pass_summary: All 6 tasks are implemented and every Goal-Verification truth is backed by a real, behaviourally-red-able test — including all nine defects flagged in plan review (live-set index predicate, slot-0 reservation, NULL-slot safety, BEGIN IMMEDIATE atomicity, non-throwing reconcile, rollback of both worktree and DB row, never-overwrite .env, tier-3 tracked-.gitignore refusal, monorepo discovery). One genuine concurrency defect remains: the lazy `ensureSlot` allocation on the detect path repeats the exact non-atomic read-then-write shape the plan mandated be wrapped in a transaction, and can throw a raw SQLITE_CONSTRAINT from a read-shaped call.

issues.title: Lazy slot allocation in `ensureSlot` is non-atomic and can throw SQLITE_CONSTRAINT from the read-only detect path
issues.description: `src/worktree/manager.ts` `ensureSlot()` does `tryAllocateSlot(...)` (SELECT via `store.listLiveSlots`) and then `this.store.assignSlot(wt.id, slot)` (UPDATE) as two separate statements, with no `runImmediate` wrapper, no retry, and no try/catch. This is the identical read-then-write race the plan explicitly called out for the insert path ("⚠️ Allocate-then-insert is NOT atomic … Wrap allocate + insert in a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction") — and `insertWithSlot` correctly does exactly that, while this second write path does not. Two concurrent `worktree_detect` calls (CLI + MCP + sidecar all open the same DB file, and the sidecar builds a fresh manager per request) can both compute the same lowest free slot; the second `UPDATE worktrees SET slot = ?` then violates `idx_wt_slot_live` and raises a raw `SQLiteError` (`SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE`). That error propagates out of `resolveWithReconcile`, which the plan states in bold must NEVER hard-fail for slot reasons (`manager.ts` docblock: "⛔ This sits on the `worktree_detect` read path and must never throw for slot reasons"). The result is `mcpError("Error detecting worktree", …)` for a purely read-shaped question, and the pre-V12 row is left unslotted. `insertWithSlot`'s `SLOT_RACE` retry/classification machinery is bypassed entirely here.
issues.suggested_fix: In `src/worktree/manager.ts`, wrap the allocate+assign in the same transaction/retry envelope used by `insertWithSlot`: e.g. add `WorktreeStore.tryAssignFreeSlot(id, projectPath, maxActive): number | null` that runs `listLiveSlots` + `assignSlot` inside `runImmediate`, retry `SLOT_INSERT_ATTEMPTS` times on `isSlotRace(err)` (export `isSlotRace` from `src/worktree/slots.ts`), and on a lost retry budget push `noFreeSlotWarning`/a transient-race warning and return the worktree unchanged rather than throwing. At minimum, wrap `this.store.assignSlot(...)` in a try/catch that degrades to a warning. Add a test in `src/worktree/manager.test.ts` mirroring `slots.test.ts`'s staged-race pattern (competitor row committed from a second connection between the SELECT and the UPDATE) asserting `resolveWithReconcile` does not throw.

issues.title: `SLOT_EXHAUSTED` IS reachable from `create()`; the in-code comment asserting otherwise is wrong and the path is untested
issues.description: `src/worktree/manager.ts` (create, inside the rollback envelope) states: "`create()` checks countActive against the same bound at :84-90, so the pool can never be empty here — SLOT_EXHAUSTED is unreachable via this path and a caller who hits the cap sees MAX_ACTIVE instead." That is false. `WorktreeStore.countActive` counts only `status = 'active'`, while `listLiveSlots` (correctly) covers `('active','ready-to-merge')`. With `maxActive: 3`: create three worktrees (slots 1,2,3), move two to `ready-to-merge` → `countActive` is 1 so the MAX_ACTIVE guard passes, but `findFreeSlot` sees `[1,2,3]` and `onExhausted: "throw"` raises `SLOT_EXHAUSTED`, and the catch tears down the just-created git worktree. The plan's own Context section anticipated this asymmetry ("`countActive` counts only 'active' … the slot design amplifies it") but Task 3 then wrote the DoD as "the 4th fails with MAX_ACTIVE, not SLOT_EXHAUSTED" and the plan told the implementer "Do not write a create()-path exhaustion test; it can never go red." The thrown error is arguably the right behaviour (its message names merge/abandon/worktree_cleanup), but the comment misleads future maintainers and the reachable branch has zero coverage.
issues.suggested_fix: Correct the comment in `src/worktree/manager.ts` to say SLOT_EXHAUSTED is reachable when `ready-to-merge` rows hold slots that `countActive` does not count, and add a `manager.test.ts` case under `describe("slots") > describe("create()")` with `testConfig.maxActive: 3` that fills the pool with `ready-to-merge` rows and asserts `create()` throws `WorktreeError` with code `SLOT_EXHAUSTED` (not `SLOT_RACE`) and that the git worktree directory was rolled back. Optionally change the MAX_ACTIVE guard to count the live set so the two bounds agree.

issues.title: Seeding/slot warnings are silently dropped in sidecar mode — the "warn loudly" mitigation does not hold on the default detect path
issues.description: `src/worktree/mcp-tools.ts` `worktree_detect` only collects warnings on the direct path: `const wt = client ? await client.resolveWorktreeBySlug(...) : manager.resolveWithReconcile(plan_slug, projectPath, warnings)`. In sidecar mode (`SidecarClient.connect()` succeeding is the normal production configuration — see `src/sidecar/*`), `/worktree/resolve` returns a bare `Worktree` with no warnings channel, so `noFreeSlotWarning`, `skipExistingWarning`, `notIsolatedWarning`, `noSeedSourceWarning` and `unexcluded`/tier-3 warnings produced by the sidecar's own `resolveWithReconcile` → `seedNonFatally` are computed and discarded. Task 5's Rule 2 ("If no `.env.example` is found → warn loudly, never silently. Silence is what drives the agent back to copying the root `.env`") and R11's not-isolated warning are therefore unenforced on the most common detect path. Task 6 discloses this as a known gap, but it defeats the phase's stated purpose rather than being cosmetic. `worktree_create` is unaffected (no sidecar route exists), so the create path is safe.
issues.suggested_fix: Extend `/worktree/resolve` in `src/sidecar/worktree-routes.ts` to return `{ worktree, warnings }` (or add a `warnings` field alongside the serialised `Worktree`), thread it through `SidecarClient.resolveWorktreeBySlug` in `src/sidecar/client.ts`, and pass it into `withWarnings(...)` in `src/worktree/mcp-tools.ts`. Add a case to `src/sidecar/worktree-routes.test.ts` asserting a warning survives the round trip, plus a `mcp-tools.test.ts` sidecar-mode case.

issues.title: An unreadable `.env.example` destroys the freshly-created worktree; the plan scoped the throwing case to write failures
issues.description: `src/worktree/worktree-config.ts` `seedWorktreeConfig` does an unguarded `readFileSync(join(repoRoot, sourceRel), "utf-8")` inside the per-source loop. The plan's failure semantics are explicit: "Missing `.env.example` / slot-free `.env.example` → warn and continue" vs "**I/O failure while writing** → throw". A seed source that `existsSync` finds during discovery but that cannot be read (permissions, a dangling symlink, a TOCTOU delete between `discoverSeedSources` and the loop) currently throws, and `create()`'s catch then runs `git worktree remove --force` plus `store.delete(id)` — the user loses an otherwise-healthy worktree over a source file Sentinal only ever wanted to copy. A missing source is treated as benign; an unreadable one is functionally the same condition.
issues.suggested_fix: In `src/worktree/worktree-config.ts`, wrap the `readFileSync` of the seed source in try/catch, push a warning modelled on `noSeedSourceWarning` naming the specific unreadable path, and `continue`. Keep the `write(...)` call unguarded so genuine write failures still throw into the rollback envelope. Add a `worktree-config.test.ts` case (a `.env.example` that exists per `existsSync` but whose read fails) asserting `seedWorktreeConfig` does not throw and emits a warning.

issues.title: `formatSlot(null)` always reads "pre-V12 worktree" even when the real cause was an exhausted slot pool
issues.description: `src/worktree/slots.ts` `formatSlot` returns the fixed string `"not assigned (pre-V12 worktree)"` for any nullish slot. But `slot = null` has a second, operationally very different origin that this phase introduces deliberately: `insertWithSlot({ onExhausted: "null" })` in `resolveWithReconcile`, and `ensureSlot` failing to find a free slot. A user or LLM reading `- **Slot:** not assigned (pre-V12 worktree)` on a worktree created five minutes ago is told a false cause and pointed at no remedy. The accompanying `noFreeSlotWarning` carries the truth, but only on the direct (non-sidecar) path — see the warnings-drop issue above — so in sidecar mode the misleading string is the only signal the caller gets.
issues.suggested_fix: In `src/worktree/slots.ts`, neutralise the wording, e.g. `"not assigned (pre-V12 record, or no free slot — see warnings)"`, or give `formatSlot` an optional reason argument. Update the corresponding assertions in `src/worktree/slots.test.ts` (`formatSlot` cases) and `src/worktree/mcp-tools.test.ts` ("renders an unassigned slot as prose, never the token `null`") — keep the existing invariant that the literal token `null` never appears.

issues.title: Workspace glob scan can descend into `node_modules` before filtering, on the `create()` hot path
issues.description: `src/worktree/worktree-config.ts` `workspacePackageDirs` builds `${pattern}/package.json` and runs `new Bun.Glob(glob).scanSync({ cwd: repoRoot })`, filtering out `node_modules` only *after* the scan returns. Workspace patterns such as `packages/**` or `apps/**` (both legal in npm/pnpm workspaces) expand to `packages/**/package.json`, which walks every installed dependency's `package.json` in a large monorepo — precisely the project shape issue #2's reporter describes — on every `worktree create` and on every lazy-allocation reconcile. There is a `try/catch { continue }` so it degrades rather than fails, but a multi-second stall inside `create()`'s rollback envelope is a poor experience.
issues.suggested_fix: In `src/worktree/worktree-config.ts`, pass a `node_modules` exclusion to the scan if the installed Bun version supports it, or cap traversal by rejecting patterns containing `**` (falling back to a single-level `<pattern>/package.json` expansion). Add a `discoverSeedSources` test with a `packages/**` pattern and a populated `node_modules` fixture to lock the behaviour in.

issues.title: Reconcile can leave `.env` and `.sentinal/worktree.env` disagreeing about the slot without detecting it
issues.description: `readSlotFromWorktree` correctly makes the directory's own env file the preferred recovery slot in `resolveWithReconcile`, but `insertWithSlot` silently falls back to `findFreeSlot` when that preferred slot is taken or out of range. Meanwhile `seedNonFatally` → `seedWorktreeConfig` skips the existing `.env` (Rule 0, correct) but unconditionally overwrites `.sentinal/worktree.env` with the newly-allocated slot. The directory then holds a `.env` interpolated against slot N and a slot file declaring slot M — the exact port/database collision the phase exists to prevent, reachable through a plain `worktree_detect`. `skipExistingWarning` fires, but it says only that `.env` "may therefore point at the wrong resources"; nothing compares the two values or states that they are known to differ.
issues.suggested_fix: In `src/worktree/manager.ts` `resolveWithReconcile`, compare `readSlotFromWorktree(onDisk.path)` against `reregistered.slot` and, when both are non-null and differ, push a dedicated warning naming both numbers and the remedy (delete `.env` and re-run, or free slot N). Add a `manager.test.ts` case that occupies the on-disk slot before reconciling and asserts the mismatch warning.

truths.evidence: `migrateV12` in `src/memory/migrations.ts` guards on the worktrees table, then `ALTER TABLE worktrees ADD COLUMN slot INTEGER`; `migrations-v12.test.ts` "adds a slot column to the worktrees table" asserts presence and INTEGER type, and "is idempotent" asserts exactly one such column after re-running.

Diff shows `SCHEMA_VERSION: 11 → 12`; `migrations-v12.test.ts` "bumps SCHEMA_VERSION to 12" asserts both the constant and `MAX(version)` in the DB. The version bump is gated behind re-verifying both the column and `idx_wt_slot_live` exist (the V11 unconditional-bump bug was deliberately not copied), and "does not bump to 12 when the worktrees table is missing" proves the guard leaves the version at 11 so the migration retries.

truths.truth: Creating two worktrees in one project yields two distinct slots, neither of which is 0
truths.evidence: `slots.ts` `findFreeSlot` iterates from `FIRST_ALLOCATABLE_SLOT = 1`; `MAIN_CHECKOUT_SLOT = 0` is never returned and `isAllocatableSlot` rejects it. Covered by `slots.test.ts` "findFreeSlot never returns 0, even when nothing is taken", "allocateSlot never returns 0 across a full pool lifetime", "ignores an out-of-range or reserved preferred slot", and end-to-end by `manager.test.ts` "gives two worktrees in one project distinct slots, neither of them 0". `readSlotFromWorktree` also refuses to adopt 0 from disk.

truths.truth: With `maxActive: 3`, three worktrees receive slots 1, 2, 3 and the fourth fails with `MAX_ACTIVE` (not `SLOT_EXHAUSTED`)
truths.evidence: `manager.test.ts` "allocates 1..maxActive, and the (maxActive+1)th fails with MAX_ACTIVE — never SLOT_EXHAUSTED", plus `slots.test.ts` "capacity is unchanged by the reservation — maxActive 3 yields slots 1..3". Note: this holds only while all held slots belong to `active` rows — see the should_fix on `ready-to-merge` making `SLOT_EXHAUSTED` reachable from `create()`.

truths.truth: Abandoning a worktree frees its slot for reuse by the next `create`
truths.evidence: Release is emergent from the `idx_wt_slot_live` predicate — no code writes `slot = NULL`. `migrations-v12.test.ts` "frees a slot when a live row transitions to abandoned" proves it at the DB level; `slots.test.ts` "frees the slot when a row becomes abandoned/merged/DELETED outright" at the store level; `manager.test.ts` `describe("release is emergent — one test per exit path")` covers abandon/squashMerge/cleanup and the remaining exit paths, with "abandon() frees the slot, and the next create() gets it" asserting reuse.

truths.truth: 5b. A `ready-to-merge` worktree does NOT free its slot — it is still live on disk
truths.evidence: The predicate is `WHERE status IN ('active', 'ready-to-merge')` in `migrateV12`, mirrored exactly by `store.listLiveSlots` and by `LIVE_WORKTREE_STATUSES` in `src/worktree/types.ts`. Crucially the proof is behavioural, not just SQL-text: `migrations-v12.test.ts` "rejects two ready-to-merge rows sharing a slot" and "rejects one active + one ready-to-merge sharing a slot" both go RED against an `active`-only predicate, as does "rejects an UPDATE that moves a row into the live set onto a taken slot". `slots.test.ts` "counts ready-to-merge as LIVE — its slot is not reallocated" and "⛔ does NOT free the slot of a ready-to-merge worktree" confirm it through the allocator.

truths.truth: The worktree `.env` contains the allocated slot at every position `.env.example` had `${SENTINAL_WORKTREE_SLOT}`, with no unsubstituted `${` token
truths.evidence: `interpolateSlot` uses `text.split(PLACEHOLDER).join(String(slot))` (all occurrences) and deliberately leaves unrelated `${...}` tokens alone; `worktree-config.test.ts` "substitutes EVERY occurrence, leaving no placeholder behind", "leaves unrelated ${...} tokens alone", and "seeds .env from .env.example with the slot substituted at every position". Rule 0 is enforced by an `existsSync` check before every write and covered three ways ("NEVER overwrites an existing worktree .env — skips and reports", "is safe to re-run", plus the reconcile path); the slotless case is covered by "a SLOTLESS worktree does not write a bogus slot into .env either". Monorepo discovery covers `package.json workspaces` (array and `{packages:[]}`) and `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, excluding `node_modules`.

truths.truth: Neither the seeded `.env` nor the slot env file appears in `git status` inside the worktree, and the main checkout's ignore behaviour is unchanged
truths.evidence: `git-exclude.ts` implements the spike's three tiers with zero common-dir writes; tier 3 explicitly refuses to touch a tracked `.gitignore` (`isTracked(worktreePath, ignoreRel)` → `unexcluded` + `trackedIgnoreWarning`) and the outcome is verified rather than assumed via a post-write `isIgnored` check. Proven by `git-exclude.test.ts` "tier 3 — REFUSES to modify a tracked .gitignore and reports the path as unexcluded" and "never writes into the common dir — the main checkout is byte-unchanged", by `worktree-config.test.ts` "leaves `git status` clean inside the worktree and the main checkout untouched" and "with a TRACKED root .gitignore it reports .env as visible, but still hides the slot file", and by the Task 1 spike (`worktree-exclude.test.ts`, incl. the two REJECTED candidates). The directory-scoped `.sentinal/.gitignore` keeps the slot env file excludable even under tier 3; the residual tier-3 `.env` visibility is a documented, warned accepted limitation.
